_comment: Two version numbers, and they are independent axes. `version` is this
contract: it bumps when a rule, a threshold or a gate_io row changes.
`release.ships_with` is the release line of the skill package that
bundles this contract. The release bumps for prose and gate-behaviour
changes too, so the two only coincide when the contract happens to move.
Recorded here because nobody can tell from the numbers alone whether
1.2.4 is newer or older than 1.0.6. A deployed copy that can name both
can prove it matches the release the README describes.
1.3.1 -> 1.3.2 puts one exit_codes["2"] trigger back in its row: the
rule-set refusal, schemas/report-contract.json missing or not parseable.
1.2.4 added it together with gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set, and
the sibling key survived; the 1.2.6 rewrite of exit_codes["2"] dropped
only the wording, so a reader who trusted that flat list had lost the
earliest of the four import-time refusals. checks/contract.py reads the
JSON as its first act, and a wrong relative path is the easiest way to
reach it. No rule, no threshold and no other row moves, so the gate
behaves exactly as it did at 1.3.1: this is a documentation fix, which is
why 1.2.4's note below could call this a gap that 'needs a reader, not a
test'.
ships_with moves to 1.1.4 because the contract that ships changes, though
no gate behaviour does. A deployed copy names both numbers, and 1.1.3's
archive would otherwise carry a contract whose own table disagrees with
the row it was written to describe.
1.1.4 -> 1.1.5 moves ships_with again with no contract change at all: the
release picks up four fixes to scripts/docgen.py, which ships but is not
part of this contract, and gains the test suite that would have caught
them. _find_block_end required the subprogram name after the end keyword,
which ABAP permits but never requires, so nothing matched, every block ran
to the end of the file, and `end` came back identical for every
subprogram. CALL FUNCTION names were read from [A-Z0-9_], which missed the
quoted form that is the common one in ABAP. A FORM's USING clause was
grouped into the FORM regex with `.*?`, which matched empty, so no FORM
ever reported a parameter. Internal tables were filtered with a
case-sensitive startswith, so lt_tab and ws_data read as database tables.
The anchored patterns indented with `\s*`, which also matches a newline, so
a subprogram preceded by a blank line anchored one line early.
version stays at 1.3.2: no rule, no threshold and no row moved.
1.1.5 -> 1.1.6 moves ships_with again with no contract change at all: the
release picks up eight fixes to scripts/abap_deps_analyzer.py, which ships
but is not part of this contract, and makes references/example-report.md
pass the gate with its own source. row-src had never been exercised on the
exemplar, because both tests that guard it ran the gate without a source --
and row-src is the one rule that only runs when a source is passed. A third
change is in the gate's documentation, not its rules: SKILL.md's exit-code
table named eight of this contract's fifteen defect prefixes and described
--fidelity-only's output wrongly, and its exit-2 table was missing several
of the gate's refusals, including report-and-source-being-the-same-file and
the three --fix output-path refusals. version stays at 1.3.2: no rule, no
threshold and no row moved.
1.1.6 -> 1.1.7 moves ships_with with no contract change at all: four fixes
to SKILL.md's prose and one to references/README.md, all found by running
the skill on two real programs. enc was in the exit-code table with no prose
anywhere, so a writer hitting a U+FFFD from a truncated multibyte character
had no way to know the fix is a re-save rather than a delete. SKILL.md claimed
both the authz and ext-asset notes go silent once the report answers them;
only authz does -- ext_asset_note returns a note whenever a bitmap or icon
literal exists, and says so in its own docstring. authz's silence bar is a
ten-keyword regex the writer could not see, so SKILL.md names it. Step 5 gains
a pre-check for those two notes, which can never be answered in steps 6 or 7
because both forbid changing the analysis and --fix only repairs ln and mm.
references/README.md now states that abap-syntax is 8 of about 30 upstream
cheat sheets, because 13 of their internal cross-links point at siblings that
were never vendored. version stays at 1.3.2: no rule, no threshold and no
row moved.
1.1.7 -> 1.1.8 moves ships_with with no contract change at all: the release
vendors one upstream cheat sheet and corrects the index that claimed it was
missing. The gap was real and load-bearing: SKILL.md told the writer to look
up syntax behaviour in abap-syntax and forbade inventing it elsewhere, while
references/README.md said the directory is a partial vendoring and that any
semantics absent from it are absent from it -- so a topic that fell between
had no permitted route. LOOP AT ... GROUP BY was exactly such a topic: it is
the one statement whose behaviour is defined by which binding form is used,
and 11_Internal_Tables_Grouping.md is the upstream sheet that documents the
representative and explicit key bindings, the INTO addition, GROUP INDEX and
GROUP SIZE, WITHOUT MEMBERS, and the member loop. It is now vendored, copied
verbatim, and verified against the upstream git blob SHA-1
3080642a8dba2d4f13208048c3e712a069ddbf9e, as are the other eight.
Verifying the archive instead of the working tree fails, and for a reason worth
recording: core.autocrlf=input normalised upstream's eight CRLF sheets to LF
when they were committed, so the shipped blobs do not match the upstream blobs
and only 27_Exceptions.md, already LF upstream, does. That is line-ending
normalisation, not edited content, and the index now says so -- otherwise a
reader who unpacks the release and compares would read it as tampering.
The index now names 9 of upstream's 37 sheets, records the Apache-2.0
provenance, and lists the twelve sibling files the cross-links still reach for.
Vendoring it added one new broken sibling link, 02_Structures.md, and removed
one, so the count of unique missing filenames stays at twelve. No reference
file is read by the gate, which reads only this contract, so version stays
at 1.3.2: no rule, no threshold and no row moved.
1.3.2 -> 1.3.3 is documentation-only, and it moves version for once: every row here
describes what the gate prints, and three of them were wrong. defect_line_prefixes
named SUBSTANTIVE and PUNCT-ONLY, but report() truncates the tier with tier[:6], so
the line that starts a fidelity defect is SUBSTA and the punctuation one is PUNCT- --
a reader grepping the documented form finds nothing. exit_codes["0"] said no shape
defect was found, which is not sufficient: report() returns 0 only when not bad and
not n_sub, and n_sub counts the fidelity SUBSTANTIVE findings, which shape mode also
prints and also counts in N. A shape-clean report with one fabricated quote exits 1,
so step 7 could return 1 for a report the writer believed was done. exit_codes["1"]
said the verdict is last in shape mode; it is not -- the notes print after FAIL and
after PASS, up to seven of them, including the one announcing that five diagnostics
never ran. And advisories[fidelity] said enforcement is note, when the substantive
tier is a defect line: 1.0.8 introduced the two tiers and this row was never
updated, the same shape as the authz keyword list SKILL.md carried until 1.1.9,
where the documented list did not match the regex. Behaviour did not change, but
version moves anyway, because the wrong text is in the contract and the contract is
what a deployed copy proves itself with.
1.1.9 -> 1.1.10 moves ships_with with no contract change at all: version stays at
1.3.3, because no rule, no threshold and no row moved. One sentence in the
shipped README was wrong, and it was wrong in a way this contract's own drift
suite can never see. It called tests/test_skill.py self-contained and free of
project data, and said the same in the runbook. From the repository root that
holds, and the 169 checks the suite carried then all pass. From the installed location it does not: every
suite resolves its fixtures by walking up from tests/ to a repository root and
then looking for sibling Test-source/ and analyzing-programs-workspace/, neither
of which ships with the package. test_skill.py goes 168 of 169 there and the
one that fails is the exemplar's source-is-present check, the row-src guard,
which needs Test-source/real/. The other four die on their first fixture.
The gate itself and its scripts are unaffected: report_qc.py on the shipped
exemplar returns 0 and prints PASS from the installed location, measured.
So the 419 checks were a repository-side claim, and the README says so,
instead of implying a deployer can re-verify the release on the machine that
consumes it.
1.1.10 -> 1.1.11 moves ships_with with no contract change at all: version stays
at 1.3.3, because no rule, no threshold and no row moved. 1.1.10 documented that
tests/ cannot run from the package; 1.1.11 stops shipping it. The harness moves
out of the archive through a NOT_SHIPPED list in release/pack.py, which asserts
a CRITICAL tuple of schemas/, scripts/, references/ and evals/ alongside it so
that putting one of those four in the exclusion list fails the pack instead of
quietly dropping a directory the gate reads. Nothing in this contract moves, and
nothing in the gate changes: the five suites were never imported by scripts/ and
read no contract key, so the archive is smaller by exactly five files and behaves
identically. Two cross-references to tests/ remain in references/README.md and
evals/README.md; they point at the repository-side suite and are left alone.
1.3.4 -> 1.3.5 moves version, because gate behaviour changes: exit 2 now
holds in every mode, not only in the shape-mode branch where its guard
had been written.
1.3.1 added the detector-crash trigger and its text says "in every mode",
and SKILL.md says so too, but the guard was added around the shape-mode
check loop and the other two branches called their detectors bare. Injecting
a RuntimeError showed --fidelity-only exiting 1 with a traceback and --fix
exiting 1 with a traceback after it had already rewritten the output file --
both read as "the check ran and found defects", which is the one false
reassurance this script exists not to give, and --fix wrote the result of an
unchecked run to disk. The guard is now run_detector(), one copy, and all
three branches go through it; putting the message in the helper is what makes
the next bare call site findable, because a per-branch copy is how this one
went undocumented.
conclusion_lines also gains PASS  <name>  (N punctuation-only): --fidelity-only
prints it when the only findings are advisory, the verdict still reads PASS and
the exit is still 0, and it was the one emittable line not on the list, so a
reader classifying output by conclusion_lines met a line the contract had never
named. exit_codes["1"] now says so, and test_skill.py constructs the case --
one space moved inside a parenthesis -- and matches the whole line, so dropping
the count is caught too.
Two rows in gate_io disagreed with the gate before 1.3.5, and neither is wrong
about anything a reader needs: source_is_optional.verdict_still_printed said
"three diagnostics" where the note and needs_source say five, and
diagnostics.enforcement said "note -- never changes the exit code" while
advisories[fidelity].enforcement says its SUBSTANTIVE tier does. The second is
the drift that matters: fidelity is listed under diagnostics, so read straight
through it reads as advisory only. Both are corrected, and enforcement now
names the exception instead of ignoring it.
ships_with moves to 1.1.13: the gate behaves differently, so a deployed copy
that names 1.3.4 is carrying the hole.
1.3.3 -> 1.3.4 moves version, because gate behaviour changes: --fix now returns 1
for a substantive rewrite, not only for the shape defects it left behind.
fidelity_report() was already being called in the --fix branch, but n_sub fed only
the notes, and the return was `1 if left else 0` where left is the shape check -- so
a shape-clean report with one fabricated quote exited 0 and printed PASS out of
--fix while exiting 1 with a FAIL out of shape mode. exit_codes["0"] already said a
rewrite blocks 0, so this contract and the gate disagreed, and step 7 loops on the
exit code, so the loop could stop on a fabricated quote.
The fidelity computation moved above the verdict; the note order did not move, which
is what notes_follow_the_verdict below asserts and test_contract_drift.py pins. The
verdict now names the two kinds separately rather than one count, so a reader can tell
that nothing mechanical was left versus that a quote still needs the model.
ships_with moves to 1.1.12: the gate behaves differently, so a deployed copy that
names 1.3.3 is carrying the hole.
1.3.0 -> 1.3.1 adds one exit_codes["2"] trigger: an unhandled exception in
a detector. It arrived with 1.1.3, which fixes inventory() for the event
blocks -- ANCHORS gives the six of them no capture group because the
keyword is the name, and inventory() took group 1 from every entry, so any
report checked against the 17 shipped sources that declare one crashed with
a traceback and exited 1, the defect verdict. Step 7 loops on a nonzero
exit, so the model edited a report whose defects did not exist. The check
loop now refuses through die(), the way the rule set and the checks import
already did. ships_with moves to 1.1.3 because gate behaviour changed; the
1.1.2 archive still carries this contract at 1.3.0.
1.1.3 also corrects a mislabel: the 1.1.2 archive declares version 1.1.1 in
its own SKILL.md frontmatter, so a deployed copy could not prove it was
1.1.2 by reading itself.
1.2.6 -> 1.3.0 adds five rule keys and nothing else changes:
problem_section.rows_require_source_object, layers.distinct,
encoding.replacement_char, mermaid.required_diagrams and
sections_exactly_once. They were declared before the detectors that
read them, so a reader of 1.3.0 alone would have believed the gate was
unchanged; they are all enforced now, as row-src, layer-same, enc,
mm-missing and sec-dup. Declaring a threshold before the detector is
the point -- the drift suite can prove the key is present and named,
which is a claim about the contract, and separately that a detector
reads it, which is a claim about the gate. The first was impossible to
state while the key did not exist.
1.2.6 -> 1.3.0 also fills the two exit_codes["2"] rows that splitting
report_qc.py into checks/ created and this file did not record:
scripts/checks/ absent, and a module in it that will not parse. Both
refuse before main() and both print an `error` line, which is the whole
reason they have to arrive through the same door as the rule-set
refusal. The gate and the table below now say the same thing.
1.0.6 -> 1.0.7 changed no rule, no threshold and no gate_io row, so
this contract stayed at 1.2.4 and only ships_with moved. Both fixes
came from field reports on another machine: the three layers
rendered as one paragraph because SKILL.md's own compact example put
them on consecutive lines, and the first layer came out too vague to
be useful. Neither was mechanically detectable, so the drift test
had nothing to assert there either.
1.2.5 -> 1.2.6 changes no rule, no threshold and no advisory. It rewrites
exit_codes["2"] to match the gate, because that one string was the last
place where a claim about the checker had never been measured. Three
wrongnesses: it said every trigger prints a line starting with `error`
while two of them print no such line; it listed `source is empty` with no
mode, so a reader would refuse a plain-mode run that in fact takes a note
and returns the shape verdict; and it identified the gate by byte size,
which made the sentence go stale every time the file grew. The per-mode
table in SKILL.md was checked cell by cell -- all 13 agree -- and it is
the one to trust. The byte sizes are gone on purpose.
1.2.4 -> 1.2.5 adds two advisories, so that version does move. They
came out of a held-out run (zvend, 21 frozen defects, blind judging)
in which the with_skill arm lost 5 defects to the without_skill arm
and every one of them was the same shape: the report NAMED the
identifier -- a hardcoded bitmap, an IS NOT INITIAL on a range, a
missing AUTHORITY-CHECK -- and then wrote a descriptive sentence and
moved on. The code was read; the conclusion was not followed through.
No gate check can catch that, so these are notes: they put the
question in front of the writer rather than asserting a defect. Both
stay silent once the report states a consequence, because naming the
topic is not answering it.
1.2.3 -> 1.2.4: exit_codes["2"] gained the rule-set trigger, and
gate_io.gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set was added. report_qc.py
already refused; SKILL.md already taught it. The contract, which this
file exists to be the single copy of, was the only place still missing
it. test_contract_drift.py cannot catch that class of gap -- it only
asserts that skill_anchor strings appear in SKILL.md -- so a drift this
wide needs a reader, not a test.
1.3.5 -> 1.3.6 moves version, because the checks that read a source read a
file of blanks as a real one. report_qc.py tested not src.strip() while the
six source-dependent checks tested not src, so a truthy string of blanks
reached them: classify() counted zero identifiers and called every quotation
a fabrication, and row-src computed an empty flat_src instead of None, which
bypassed its own "no source given: cannot judge, so do not fail" hatch and
reported every problem row as naming nothing. The exemplar plus a blank
source printed 28 defects and exited 1, while --fidelity-only refused the
same file -- three modes, three answers for one input. What could not be
judged was reported as a judgement, the false verdict the ReadError guard
exists to stop. checks/text.py gained _src_of(), one normalisation all three
modules already import from.
Two rows also disagreed with the note. skip_note listed five checks that were
not run and needs_source listed the same five, while row-src is a sixth that
needs a source and is skipped with them; 1.3.5 caught three against five and
left the sixth out. Both are six now, and row-src is the one enforced check
in needs_source -- the rest are advisories, which is why it is named.
ships_with moves to 1.1.14: a deployed copy that names 1.3.5 scores a blank
source as 28 defects.
Machine-readable contract for what a report must contain.
This file is the source for report_qc.py's rules about report shape: which
sections, which layer labels, which priority buckets, which citation spellings
are forbidden, which Mermaid characters break a label, and how far a prose
window reaches. The checker reads them rather than hardcoding patterns, so
none of those can exist in the checker alone. ABAP construct syntax (the
ANCHORS table) stays in the checker: it describes the source, not the report,
and it is the list a repair is allowed to substitute. Each rule carries a
`skill_anchor`: a token that must also appear in
SKILL.md. test_contract_drift.py fails when a rule has no anchor in the
skill, or the skill states a constraint no rule covers.
Why this exists: seven separate fixes in this project were a checker
detector disagreeing with the rule it was supposed to enforce. LINENO
matched two spellings so `L23` scored clean; the Mermaid pattern differed
between the checking half and the fixing half; the exemplar's own snippet
guard had a quote-exemption the skill never granted. A second copy of the
rules inside the checker is the cause, so there is now only this one.

layers.prose_window: from the closing fence to the next fence of any language or the next heading -- not to the next quoted fence, which let labels inside an intervening abap-fix fence, or the label words anywhere later in the document, satisfy a block that had no prose of its own
layers.distinct_why: three layers carrying one sentence is a list, not an analysis; the labels exist but say nothing

violation_kinds.A8-pt: prose present inside that window, some labels missing

encoding.why: a truncated multi-byte character renders as U+FFFD and reads as a rendering fault in the finished report; one in exp-1.0.9/with_skill/run3.md went unnoticed for a whole round

_comment: How to read the checker. Recorded here because the ways of NOT being
checked look like passing, and because these semantics have now been
rewritten three times. The exit-code table SKILL.md taught was written
against an early gate, then against the one that refused a bad source path
instead of passing quietly and dropped the .abap suffix, then against the
one that also refuses a bad report. Byte sizes are deliberately absent:
naming them made this comment go stale every time the file grew, and the
size carried no information the exit-code table does not already state.
Every row below was measured by running the gate, not read off the source.
test_contract_drift.py only asserts the skill_anchor values appear in
SKILL.md. It does not re-derive any of this from report_qc.py, so a change
to main() has to be made here by hand.
1.3.6 changes one word and one entry in this block: row-src joins
source_is_optional.skip_note and diagnostics.needs_source, and exit_codes[2]
records that --fix now writes nothing when a detector crashes. Every other
row is untouched.

exit_codes.0: every report was checked, no shape defect was found, and there is no substantive rewrite -- fidelity SUBSTANTIVE findings also block 0, so a shape-clean report with one fabricated quote exits 1, in every mode; notes may accompany it and never change it
exit_codes.1: the check ran and found defects. Shape mode prints the defect lines first -- the shape prefixes plus one SUBSTA line per fidelity SUBSTANTIVE finding, and N counts both -- then the verdict, then the notes: the verdict is not the last line in shape mode or in --fix, notes follow it. --fidelity-only prints the tier lines first (displayed as SUBSTA and PUNCT-, six characters, truncated from the canonical names), then `FAIL  <name>  (N rewrite(s), M punctuation-only)` or `PASS  <name>` -- or `PASS  <name>  (N punctuation-only)` when the only findings are advisory, the verdict still reads PASS and the exit is still 0, and a reader who matches `PASS  <name>` exactly would miss the count -- and only there is the verdict last. --fix prints `FAIL  <name>  (<what is left> need the model)`, naming the two kinds separately -- `N shape defect(s)`, `N rewrite(s)`, or both joined by ` and ` -- then its notes, and it exits 1 for a rewrite as well: until 1.3.4 --fix returned 0 and printed PASS where shape mode returned 1 for the same report, so 0 meant two different things in two modes. The verdict names the kinds instead of one shared count, because folding shape and rewrite defects into a single N would make the fix look cosmetic while hiding which one is still to fix
exit_codes.2: refused to run, nothing was inspected. Triggers, by mode -- the mode matters and the flat list this replaced did not say so: common, the rule set could not be read -- schemas/report-contract.json is missing or not parseable JSON / the gate's own detectors did not load -- scripts/checks/ is absent or a module in it will not parse / no arguments / no .md/.markdown path among the arguments / report path does not exist; plain, more than one source / source path does not exist; --fidelity-only, the source is not exactly one (0 and 2 both refuse) / source does not exist / the source is empty / the source is not utf-8; --fix, fewer than two paths / -o with no output path; and in all three modes a file that is not utf-8, report or source. Two triggers print no `error` line: no arguments prints the usage text, and --fix with too few paths prints `--fix needs REPORT and SOURCE`. SKILL.md records both. An empty source is NOT a refusal in plain mode -- the shape can still be checked, so it takes a note and returns the shape verdict; that scoping was the second thing the flat list got wrong. The two detectors-did-not-load triggers arrived with 1.1.0's split of report_qc.py and were missing from this row until 1.3.0: the guard prints `error  cannot load the checks at <scripts dir> (<cause>), so nothing was checked` and exits 2, in every mode, because a missing checks/ otherwise raised ImportError and an unparseable one raised SyntaxError, and both exit 1 -- the defect verdict. Those two are listed first under common because they fire at import, before argv is read, so a mode can never be the thing that decides them. 1.3.1 adds a third, in every mode: an unhandled exception inside the check loop prints `error  internal error checking <report>: <type>: <msg> -- the gate crashed, so treat this report as unchecked, not as defects found` and exits 2 -- that is the event-block IndexError that shipped in 1.1.2, which printed a traceback and exited 1, and read as a FAIL. 1.3.2 restores the rule-set trigger to this row: 1.2.4 added it alongside gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set, and the 1.2.6 rewrite of this string dropped only the wording, so the flat list had silently lost the earliest of the four import-time refusals -- checks/contract.py reads the JSON before anything else in the import block can fail, and a wrong relative path is the cheapest way to reach it. Nothing else in the row changed, and the gate behaves exactly as it did at 1.3.1. 1.3.6 makes the opening clause literal in --fix as well: until then the write sat between the second detector and the three that followed it, so a crash in any of those exited 2 and said nothing had been inspected while the output file was already on disk -- and in place, where the report is usually the only copy, the refusal left a .bak to recover from. All four detectors now run before the write, so a refusal leaves no file behind.
exit_codes.why_2_is_separate: an unhandled exception exits 1, which is the code SKILL.md defines as 'the check ran and found defects', and the caller then goes and fixes defects that do not exist, or loops step 7 forever. So every refusal has to arrive through die(), including a decode failure on the report. The report side was bare at three call sites until 1.0.9: a report saved as cp936 -- what an editor's 'save as' gives on a Chinese Windows, the trap SKILL.md warns about for pasted source -- exited 1 with a traceback. The source side was guarded from the start and the rule set has its own try/except at import, so the guarantee covered one of the two files.
exit_codes.measured: 1.0.9: every cell of SKILL.md's per-mode table was run against report_qc.py, all 13 agree, and the six non-utf-8-report cases now exit 2 in all three modes. test_skill.py carries 28 checks for it. 1.3.0: the two detectors-did-not-load triggers were measured the same way, by deleting scripts/checks/ from a copy and by appending an unparseable line to checks/text.py in a copy -- both print the error line above and exit 2. 1.3.1: the detector-crash trigger was measured by reverting the inventory() fix in a copy of the tree and checking a report against a source that declares START-OF-SELECTION -- it prints the error line above and exits 2 instead of raising IndexError and exiting 1. test_skill.py carries that source as a permanent check, asserting both that no traceback is printed and that inventory() still counts all six event blocks as a denominator, so a regression that returns an empty inventory instead of crashing is caught too. 1.3.2: the rule-set trigger was re-measured on a copy of the tree, once with schemas/ removed and once with unparseable JSON written to schemas/report-contract.json -- both print the error line of gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set and exit 2, in every mode. 1.3.5: the detector-crash trigger was re-measured in all three modes at once, by injecting a RuntimeError into report_qc's detectors and running shape mode, --fidelity-only and --fix against the same report -- all three print the error line above and exit 2. Before the fix, --fidelity-only exited 1 with a traceback and --fix exited 1 with a traceback after it had already rewritten the output file, so exit 2 was enforced only in the one branch whose guard had been written. Two regressions were caught by re-running every mode instead of the one that changed: the new guard first swallowed an argument out of report() and broke the shape-mode baseline, which the baseline check caught before anything was packed. test_skill.py now carries nine checks for the guard, one for each of the three assertions in each of the three modes, and fails on --fidelity-only and --fix against the pre-fix tree. The advisory PASS form was measured by moving one space inside a parenthesis in a quoted statement -- SELECT ... INTO @DATA(ls_foo ) -- which the identity check accepts and the flattened substring check rejects, so --fidelity-only prints PASS  <name>  (1 punctuation-only) and exits 0. 1.3.6: the blank-source verdict was measured by pointing the exemplar at a file of spaces and tabs -- 28 defects and exit 1, against PASS with its own source, and an exit-2 refusal from --fidelity-only on the same file. After the fix the same call prints PASS and names what it did not measure, and --fidelity-only still refuses it. test_skill.py carries four checks for the blank source, and one per --fix detector position asserting that no crash position leaves an output file behind; against the pre-fix tree the first of those four fails and all four ordering checks fail.

gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set.where: module import, before main() and before every exit-2 guard
gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set.trigger: schemas/report-contract.json is missing or not parseable JSON
gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set.prints: error  cannot read the rule set at <path> (<cause>), so nothing was checked
gate_start_refuses_without_a_rule_set.why_not_1: an unhandled exception exits 1, which is the defect verdict; refusing by exception is the one false reassurance this script is not allowed to give, arriving through the wrong door

argument_roles.rule: a report is any path ending .md or .markdown; every other path on the command line is a source
argument_roles.why: the previous gate recognised a source by the .abap suffix, so a .txt source was neither read nor announced and was then checked as a report -- a source file with no six sections then failed the gate on defects that were never real
argument_roles.one_source_only: two sources is an error, not a silent 'use the last one', which looks like a successful run while checking one report against nothing

source_is_optional.skip_note: no source recognised, so density, fidelity, fix-mislabel, authz, ext-asset and row-src were not run (pass the ABAP file after the report)
source_is_optional.verdict_still_printed: PASS and exit 0 -- the shape verdict is real, six checks simply did not run

diagnostics.enforcement: note -- never changes the exit code, so the writer has to read them. The one exception is fidelity: its SUBSTANTIVE tier is a defect line, counted in N and in the exit code, not a note, so this row does not cover it. That is advisories[fidelity].enforcement, and the two rows disagreeing is how a reader would read fidelity as advisory-only

gate_io.fence_sorts_first: an unclosed fence swallows the rest of the document, so nothing after it is inspected at all; fixing anything else before fixing that is wasted
conclusion_lines: FAIL  <name>  (N shape defect(s) need the model)
FAIL  <name>  (N shape defect(s) and M rewrite(s) need the model)
gate_io.notes_follow_the_verdict: in shape mode and in --fix the verdict is followed by up to seven notes, so a reader who reads only the last line misses them all -- including the note announcing that five diagnostics never ran. Only --fidelity-only ends on its verdict
gate_io.fix_writes_a_backup: --fix saves the previous text next to the report as <report>.bak before rewriting in place, and preserves the report's own CRLF/LF endings. Only when repairs actually happened: the guard is `if dest == rep and n`, so a no-op --fix still rewrites the report in place but writes no backup
gate_io.skill_anchor: 退出码是唯一的机器判据

advisories.why: a report can satisfy every rule above and still be a list rather than an analysis

advisories.enforcement: PUNCT-ONLY is a note; SUBSTANTIVE is a defect line counted in N and in the exit code

tiers.SUBSTANTIVE: a defect line, counted in the FAIL total and in the exit code -- it blocks exit 0 in every mode, including the shape-only steps 6 and 7
tiers.PUNCT-ONLY: a note only, never changes the exit code; filtered out of the shape-mode defect count

advisories.display_prefix: the gate prints tier[:6], so the canonical names appear as the six characters SUBSTA and PUNCT-
advisories.why: a fabricated block keeps six sections, three layers and four buckets; nothing structural sees it

fence language is the only admission test, but a proposed fix left in an abap fence is probed against the source and reads as fabricated; the exemption used to be positional and skipped the next sub-step's real quote as well -- 12 of 138 quoted statements uninspected on one report

a program that reads data but never checks authorization is a real question, not automatically a finding: reports run under S_TCODE, so anyone who can execute already may see the output. The note therefore asks rather than asserts, and it stays silent when the source does read data and has an AUTHORITY-CHECK. Scoped to data-reading sources so a program that touches no data is not flagged -- a note nobody reads is worse than no note
advisories.answered_when_report_states: a consequence, not the topic. Naming the absence ('no permission check') is not answering it; the question is what follows from it. Measured on a real report that said '不做权限控制' and was still judged partial for not saying who can then see the data

advisories.why: bitmaps, icons and OData service names live in the target system, not in the source, so naming one as a literal creates a dependency that no compiler and no syntax check can see; the failure appears at run time. Reports the names and the count of TRY/EXCEPTIONS guards in the source, and asks whether each call site is inside one

abap and abap-fix locked in only one direction: a fix left in an abap fence is probed and reads as fabricated, but source pasted into an abap-fix fence is never compared with the source at all, so the language tag could be used to opt a quote out of the check that exists to catch invented quotes
advisories.criterion: contiguity, not membership. An abap-fix fence is called out when its statements, flattened and joined, occur as one adjacent run in the source. The first version asked whether every statement occurs anywhere; it fired five times across nine real reports and all five were genuine fixes (a CALL FUNCTION with EXCEPTIONS added, a DELETE followed by an sy-subrc check, a restructured TRY block) whose lines each exist somewhere in a 1600-line file. Quoting the line you are about to change is legitimate, so membership cannot be the test; a mislabeled quote is a verbatim copy, and a verbatim copy is adjacent.

_comment: Where the checker runs is itself a measured rule, not a style preference.
Run inside generation, the gate costs defect recall: -0.250 at twenty
defects with an exact sign test p=0.0215, and -0.224 at thirty-eight, the
same sign at two resolutions. Run as a separate pass after the analysis
is final, recall returns to a level 0.035 from the no-checker arm while
transcription accuracy is still gained.
What the loop checks makes no difference. An arm that checked only
quotations and an arm that checked everything scored identically, p=1.0.
The cost is the loop occupying writing budget, which section 3 needs. So
the rule is not 'check less' -- it is 'check at a different moment', and a
repair pass may not touch the analysis.
loop_position.magnitude_is_unmeasured: The two deltas below are recorded as measured, but the cells are too few for the effect size: a later three-run arm retracted the point estimate as noise. Direction only -- two resolutions, same sign -- is what the skill teaches, and no percentage appears in SKILL.md.
loop_position.transcription_errors_attribution: The eight errors cited in an earlier draft came from the arm that checked fidelity DURING generation; the post-write arm found two. Neither number belongs to the loop-position rule -- transcription accuracy is the fidelity diagnostic's effect, so SKILL.md now says 'two to eight depending on the arm' and attributes it to the diagnostic.

_comment: Passing a deterministic check licenses only the claim that the shape is
right. It says nothing about whether the analysis is correct, and nothing
about whether anything was missed. archify states this as a rule --
passing one claim never implies the others -- so it is written down here
rather than left to the reader to infer from the tool names.
claim_separation.deterministic_checks_establish: the report has the required shape and quotes source faithfully
claim_separation.requires_a_named_reviewer_for: whether the analysis is correct and what it missed
claim_separation.reviewer_mechanism: scripts/evaluate.py against a frozen defect list in evals/
